🚨🇲🇽 SOFI STADIUM WORKERS — 96% AUTHORIZE STRIKE OVER ICE ONE WEEK BEFORE WORLD CUP

About 2,000 hospitality workers at SoFi Stadium — cooks, dishwashers, cashiers, bartenders — voted 96% to authorize a strike a week before the US plays Paraguay there on June 12, the World Cup's opening US-soil match. Their core demand to FIFA: keep ICE off the stadium grounds and out of their personal data. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin tried to spin it on Fox News, claiming agents would be at the matches "not for immigration but for terrorist threats" — his Acting Assistant Secretary refused to confirm that on the record. Workers, many of whom are immigrants, don't buy it. The empire that demands Mexico hand fentanyl enforcement to the DEA can't even guarantee its own stadium staff won't get snatched on the clock.

🚨🇲🇽 AMERICAN SOCIETY PROPOSES "TLCC" — A US-MEXICO SECURITY TREATY BOLTED ONTO T-MEC

At American Society of Mexico's gala dinner June 7 — held under the cover of the 250th anniversary of US independence — president Larry Rubin unveiled a "Tratado de Lucha Contra el Crimen" (TLCC) between Mexico and the US, pitching it as the security sequel to NAFTA. "Just as the trade agreement transforms how our economies collaborate, we need a new level of cooperation to face together those who threaten security and prosperity," Rubin told a room stacked with PRIAN politicians, Ricardo Salinas Pliego, and CCE president José Medina Mora. Ambassador Ronald Johnson, who had confirmed attendance, sent a video message instead and ducked the optics. Sheinbaum has rejected this framing every week for two months. The script: graft a security pact onto T-MEC review and hand cartel enforcement to Washington.

🇲🇽🚆 An electric car for México, from México — 150,000 pesos, 125 km per charge, wheelchair-accessible. "This is Olinia 1, an accessible electric vehicle, low-cost and designed for the daily life of millions of Mexicans." — Roberto Capuano Tripp, Director of the Olinia Project — Zumpango, Estado de México The numbers: 49 centavos per kilometer to operate — 5x cheaper than gasoline, less than half a motorcycle. Six passengers, anchor for wheelchair users, IP67 water-resistant motor and battery, charges from any household outlet. 50% Mexican content at launch, target 75% by 2030. First deliveries summer 2027.

🇲🇽✊ "When México trusts the intelligence and creativity of its people, there is no limit that can stop it." "Olinia is not just an electric vehicle. Olinia is a simple but very powerful idea: that the intelligence and creativity of young Mexicans can become innovation, technological development, and wellbeing for our people." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, with the Olinia engineering team — Zumpango, Estado de México 18 months ago none of this existed. Today, engineers from 22 Mexican states — drawn from public universities, the Politécnico, the TecNM and four SECIHTI research centers — handed President Sheinbaum the keys to Olinia 1, designed and built in México.

🇲🇽🏭 "México was made only for the maquila." That's what they told us. That's false. "For a long time, México was talked about as a country destined only to produce what others imagined. They told us 'we couldn't,' that 'we shouldn't.' They told us 'innovation was reserved for other places.' That 'México was made only for the maquila.' That our role was 'to receive technology, not to develop it' — 'to receive ideas, not to create them.' But that's false." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, presenting Olinia 1 in Zumpango, Estado de México Olinia — "movement" in Náhuatl — is a 100% Mexican-designed electric vehicle: 6 seats, wheelchair-accessible, 125+ km range per charge, starting at 150,000 pesos. First deliveries summer 2027.

🇲🇽🎨 "That capacity to create and transform does not belong to the past." President Sheinbaum, presenting Olinia today, on where Mexican innovation has always lived: "Esa capacidad de imaginar, de crear y de transformar no pertenece al pasado. Ha estado siempre viva, en la mejora de semillas nativas de los pequeños productores, en el uso de plantas medicinales, en la preservación de la sustentabilidad en cultivos, en nuevas mentes y manos para hacer nuevos platillos." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Base Militar de Santa Lucía, June 7 2026 Heir to civilizations that built cities and engineered solutions from observation. Today: an electric car designed by Mexican public universities.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico's first national electric car was designed with space for a wheelchair user. Rafael Garayoa, Olinia's technical director: "Por primera vez en un vehículo de esta categoría, hemos incorporado el espacio suficiente para permitir el traslado de una persona usuaria de silla de ruedas." "For the first time in a vehicle of this category, we have included enough space to allow the transport of a wheelchair user." — Rafael Garayoa, Olinia presentation, Santa Lucía, June 7 2026 Designed by public universities. Cheaper to operate than a motorcycle. State-led innovation with accessibility built in from the design table.
